clue.text: Built to last or about to break?

indicators.note: about tells us the little word or is turned round to face the other way

parts.note: taken as written before turning
to bust something is to break it

explanation.surface: A riddle asking whether something is sturdily made or on the verge of falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns OR into RO, which then goes in front of BUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sturdy and strongly made is built to last.

clue.text: Agitated, as interest is reduced by -a half

indicators.note: a half keeps just the back half of the word interest

parts.note: less means reduced, made smaller

explanation.surface: Anxiety because the interest rate has been cut by half.
explanation.walkthrough: The last half of INTEREST is REST, then LESS; 'as', 'is' and 'by' link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fidgety and unable to settle is agitated.

clue.text: Drinking establishment excluding a woman

parts.note: a bar is a place serving drinks
to bar is to exclude

explanation.surface: A pub turning a woman away.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbara is a female given name.

clue.text: Vessels capsizing, leading to fury in port

indicators.note: capsizing in a down clue turns the vessels word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: vats are large vessels for liquid
anger means fury

explanation.surface: Boats overturning, causing rage in a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsizing' turns VATS into STAV; 'leading to' puts it before ANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Stavanger is a Norwegian seaport on the North Sea coast.

clue.text: One short extract from poem, that's all

indicators.note: short asks for a word cut by its final letter, so the synonym for One loses its tail

parts.note: a unit is one single thing
a verse is a stanza taken from a poem

explanation.surface: A single brief passage quoted from a poem, and nothing more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims UNIT to UNI.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosmos is everything there is, the whole lot, so it is all that exists.

clue.text: Religious song, say, in specially devised prison ceremony

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for say inside the rearranged letters
specially devised says the letters of prison are worked into a new order

parts.note: eg (for example) is what say means here
a ritual is a ceremony

explanation.surface: A hymn, for instance, within a purpose-built jail service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specially devised' makes NROSPI from PRISON, with EG inside after the N, then RITUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the traditional term for the sacred folk songs of enslaved African Americans, a religious song form.

clue.text: Composer's decision to omit overture and finale of concert

indicators.note: to omit says letters are dropped from the decision word

parts.note: a verdict is a decision

indicators.note: the overture and finale of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A composer deciding to cut the opening and closing pieces of a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: C and T, the first and last letters of concert, are removed from VERDICT.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian opera composer of Aida and La traviata.

clue.text: A desire to forge banknotes?

indicators.note: to forge is to fashion or counterfeit, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Wanting to counterfeit money.
explanation.walkthrough: READIES is British slang for ready cash, banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: This is British slang for paper money, cash ready to hand.

clue.text: Restaurant with no cooker overlooking yard

indicators.note: overlooking in a down clue means sitting above, so the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: an eater consumes food rather than cooks it, so is no cook

explanation.surface: A restaurant without a stove, looking out over a yard.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual café or diner is a place to eat out, a restaurant.

clue.text: Holy man bringing strange solemnity into designated places

indicators.note: into says the rearranged letters go inside the places word

parts.note: sites are designated places

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters of solemnity are jumbled

explanation.surface: A saint bringing an odd seriousness to official locations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' makes MEONSTYLI from SOLEMNITY, which goes inside SITES after SI.
explanation.definitionFit: Simeon Stylites was a fifth-century Syrian ascetic saint who lived atop a pillar.

clue.text: Carol grabs the best, being hysterical?

indicators.note: grabs means the carol word holds another piece inside it

parts.note: to carol is to sing
the cream is the best part, as in the cream of the crop

explanation.surface: A singer snatching the finest part of something while in a frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name or a Christmas song but is the verb SING.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is shrieking uncontrollably is in a hysterical state.

clue.text: Slate roof half demolished on this side of a street

indicators.note: half demolished keeps only the front half of the word roof

explanation.surface: A slate roof partly knocked down on the near side of a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on this side of' simply places RO before A ST. 'Slate' looks like roofing material but is the verb meaning to criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate someone is to criticise harshly, the same as to pan or lambast them.

clue.text: Hiding in shelter, a king needs a good escape

indicators.note: the shelter word is hiding the other pieces in it, so they go inside

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, out of the wind
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch sheltering somewhere needs a successful getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: A, K, A and G all go inside LEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A leak is an unwanted escape of liquid or gas, as is a leakage.

clue.text: Famous actor one's seen in Sixties musical

indicators.note: seen in says the piece for one appears inside the title of the show

parts.note: Oliver! is Lionel Bart's 1960 stage musical, based on Oliver Twist
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's is just 'is'

explanation.surface: A celebrated actor appears in a Sixties stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Olivier was the great English stage and screen actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier is among the most renowned English actors of the twentieth century.

clue.text: A feature of Cockneys' language?

indicators.note: feature of says the answer is a part held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Asks about one of the characteristics of the speech of East Londoners.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's def 'A' was wrong: the whole clue defines, since rhyming slang is a hallmark of Cockney speech, and the letters run across cockneyS LANGuage.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang is the best-known trait of the speech of Cockneys, Londoners born within sound of Bow Bells.

clue.text: Looking after the family pets

parts.note: reads as caring for the household animals, but means favouring one's own relatives, the pets being favourites

explanation.surface: Someone tending the household's cats and dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Favouritism shown to relatives, especially in giving jobs, treats kin as favoured pets.

clue.text: Fruit with flavour Irene specially collected

parts.note: tang is a sharp flavour

indicators.note: specially collected says the letters of Irene are gathered in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Irene gathering fruit with a particular taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specially collected' turns IRENE into ERINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A small loose-skinned orange citrus is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: German booze, not English, loaded on ship

indicators.note: in a down clue, loaded on puts the first piece on top of the ship
not says the English letter is removed from the booze word

parts.note: beer is booze
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: German beer, not English, put aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: BEER without one E gives BER.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the German capital is a German from that city.

clue.text: I need to make the right connections in my business

definitions.text: I need to make the right connections in my business

parts.words: I need to make the right connections in my business
parts.note: sounds like a networker talking, but is a switchboard worker who plugs calls through

explanation.surface: A business person explaining the importance of networking.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone switchboard worker literally connects callers on the correct lines.

clue.text: Ideal trip ending with region of. Spain

indicators.note: ending picks the final letter of trip

parts.note: Aragon is a region in north-east Spain

explanation.surface: The perfect holiday finishing in a Spanish region.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a model of perfection, an ideal example.

clue.text: Husband' settles into pleasant cubby-hole

indicators.note: settles into means the husband piece goes inside the other word

parts.note: nice means pleasant
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband making himself at home in a cosy little nook.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess or nook in a wall is a small snug space, a cubby-hole.

clue.text: A' disturbance following first couple of cheer-leaders in vehicle

indicators.note: first couple of takes the opening two letters of cheer-leaders

parts.note: a riot is a disturbance

explanation.surface: Trouble breaking out after the cheerleaders' vehicle arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts A RIOT after CH.
explanation.definitionFit: A chariot is a horse-drawn two-wheeled ancient vehicle.

clue.text: A difficult thing to bear? That's not how it's seen here

definitions.text: That's not how it's seen here

parts.note: a cross to bear is a burden or affliction

explanation.surface: Remarking that a burden looks different from here.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works because this clue is a down light, not an across one.
explanation.definitionFit: This entry runs vertically in the grid, so it is not seen horizontally here.

clue.text: Artist having frame of fawn or light brown

indicators.note: the artist has the fawn word as a frame round him, so it goes inside

parts.note: camel is a fawn colour
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter putting a fawn or pale brown frame on a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fawn' looks like a young deer but is the colour CAMEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffee-coloured is a light brown shade, the colour of burnt sugar.

clue.text: Worker given less prominence in report

indicators.note: in report signals a word that sounds like another when spoken

parts.note: minor means of lesser importance

explanation.surface: An employee pushed down the ranks in an official write-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who digs coal underground is a manual worker.

clue.text: Extremity may have nasty one ingrowing

definitions.text: Extremity may have nasty one ingrowing

indicators.note: ingrowing means the scrambled piece grows into the extremity word, going inside it

parts.note: the tail is the hindmost extremity

indicators.note: nasty signals that the letters of one are rearranged

explanation.surface: A painful foot complaint where something grows inward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' turns ONE into OEN, which goes inside TAIL. The whole clue also defines: a toe's extremity can be painfully ingrowing.
explanation.definitionFit: The horny plate on a toe is an extremity notorious for growing in painfully.

clue.text: Perhaps one that's stopped the heart?

definitions.text: Perhaps one that's stopped the heart?

parts.words: Perhaps one that's stopped the heart?
parts.note: reads as something that halted a heartbeat, but the heart is one such body part and a church instrument has stops

explanation.surface: Wondering what caused a cardiac arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart is a bodily organ, and the pipe instrument has stops that control its ranks of pipes.

clue.text: Custom of banishment? Old lover has to go

parts.note: extradition sends a person out of the country to face trial
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Asking whether exile is customary, and saying a former partner must leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A custom is a practice handed down through generations, an inherited convention.

clue.text: Summer garment in miscellanea I discarded by Christmas, finally

indicators.note: discarded means the letter I is thrown out of the miscellanea word

parts.note: sundries are miscellaneous small items

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of Christmas

explanation.surface: Finding a summer outfit among odds and ends thrown out at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: SUNDRIES loses I to give SUNDRES, then S from Christmas follows; 'by' places it alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: A light sleeveless frock worn in hot weather is a garment for summer.

clue.text: Bully man caught reiterating nonsense?

parts.note: he is a male pronoun, so stands for man
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

parts.note: rot means nonsense

explanation.surface: A man caught repeating rubbish is a bully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reiterating' turns ROT into TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To hector is to browbeat or intimidate someone, as a bully does.
